s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with inflammatory signs in one eye in the context of recent severe respiratory infection
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
Mild anterior chamber inflammation and noticeable pupillary edema
key_facts: Woman in her late 50s hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia
Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history reported
Developed blurred vision and redness in one eye on day 2 post-admission
Temporary pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD and 0 logMAR OS
Normal complete blood cell counts
Normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts showed normal results

s4.champion: COVID-19-associated optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis

raw.champion: COVID-19-associated optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis
raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including blurred vision, redness, and pain in one eye, along with the presence of retinal vasculitis and optic neuritis, are consistent with this diagnosis. The positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and the temporal relationship between the COVID-19 infection and the development of ocular symptoms support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: SARS-CoV-2–associated optic neuritis
rejected.why: This option is too narrow, as it only accounts for optic neuritis, whereas the patient's symptoms and test results also indicate retinal vasculitis.

rejected.label: Post-infectious optic neuritis
rejected.why: This option is too broad and does not specifically account for the patient's COVID-19 infection or the presence of retinal vasculitis.

rejected.label: Varicella-Zoster Virus-Associated Optic Neuritis
rejected.why: The patient's serology results show negative IgM and very weakly positive IgG for VZV, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Immune-mediated parainfectious optic neuritis
rejected.why: While this option is plausible, the patient's symptoms and test results more strongly support a direct association between COVID-19 and the development of optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis.
